## WEBHOOK INTAKE & VALIDATION
Receives tweets from TwitterAPI.io webhook
- Validates API key for security
- Normalizes tweet data format

## REPLY ENRICHMENT
Fetches original tweets for replies
- Batch fetches up to 100 tweets at a time
- Adds context to reply tweets

## DATA FORMATTING
Formats tweet data for Google Sheets
- Extracts media URLs
- Structures all 14 fields

## MERGE & WRITE
Final output stage
- Merges tweets with/without media
- Writes all data to Google Sheets
- Updates existing tweets (no duplicates)

## MEDIA PROCESSING PIPELINE
Handles tweets with media attachments
- Downloads images/videos from Twitter
- Uploads to Google Drive folder
- Collects Drive links per tweet

## QUOTE TWEET ENRICHMENT
- Adds: quoted tweet ID, author, URL, full text

Remember the Executive Chairman and company that paid $40 million as the result of a tax fraud lawsuit filed by the D.C. Attorney General? The Executive Chairman openly bragged about his tax fraud scheme and called people that paid D.C. taxes “stupid.” Employees of the company were also complacent in falsifying W-2 information for the Executive Chairman. 

Remember the Executive Chairman and company that claim to have bought 700k+ Bitcoin but refuse to provide Proof of Reserves? The same company that has convinced its shareholders that diluting them to purchase Bitcoin is a real business model all the while the stock is down 75% from all time highs. 

History doesn’t repeat itself, but it often rhymes. Buffett famously said he looks for three traits: integrity, intelligence, and energy. He emphasizes that without integrity, the other two traits will destroy a company.

Are we watching the destruction play out in real time? $MSTR

tweets.text:
$PGY 

Quarter was soft and guidance soft.

Interesting thing to consider is that last time this happened (2023 ish), the company "stepped up" and kept the revenue growth engine on (I think they said it was a strategic investment in the network). The result was growth stayed high but credit losses grew enormously. The market was very displeased with that, partially because this strategy was not communicated ahead of time. AFTER the losses occurred, it was explained "this was a strategic decision to stay in the market to show our partners we're reliable etc."

This time around, with the credit market showing some signs of stress (not alarming... yet) they're intentionally pulling back, turning off the growth engine, and being conservative.

In one sense, they "learned" from the past mistake, but the question is, is it really a mistake? Large losses -> punish stock price, Slower growth -> punish stock price.

The bottom line is that they're still an "early growing business" that is exposed to the credit cycle. As they grow, build partnerships, and get leverage over their counterparties they can slowly reduce their sensitivity to the credit cycle, but it's a SLOW process.

Overall my thesis of "this is a business that might work, and their operational leverage is huge if it does work" is still there. Very high risk stock though, and it swings around with earnings in a very volatile manner (both ways).

I'm currently at a 2% weight.

profile_bio.description: Teaches economics and investing at Stanford GSB. Special sits HF mgr. https://t.co/kiKMwr0H4y || Not Financial Advice

quoted_tweet.text:
$PGY

Quarter was great, basically every financial metric is moving in the right direction.

FLRPC is now at 5% which is great to see.
Costs/expenses are under control, margins expanding.
Extra disclosure regarding their write downs so investors can get a better feel for how that looks.

We can't forget that last year was a disaster with credit-related write downs. The story is that was a one-time (18 month) episode for the company and everything is up and to the right from here. With FLRPC margins up, balance sheet usage (credit retention) down, I'm inclined to believe them.

If that's true (which I accept is something people have different levels of skepticism about), the operating leverage of the business is immense and we're regularly seeing that in the numbers.

If that's false, the business is just exposed to credit cyclicality and markets cannot give it a meaningful multiple since its profits ebb and flow instead of move consistently.

I'm getting increasingly convinced that they're in great shape and things only move up from here. It's still a very high risk stock, but I think the upside outweighs the downside.

Generally I write about PGY less these days because other contributors like @mountaingoatcap cover it better.

Currently a ~4% weight in my fund.
